speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) over the last three years, what have been the take-up rates of adult vaccinations recommended by the Ministry; and (b) how is the Ministry helping to raise awareness of adult vaccination, especially for those in the high-risk groups, such as the elderly and those with medical conditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: These vaccinations include catch-up vaccinations and vaccinations that high-risk adults should receive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: To encourage take-up, some public healthcare institutions held vaccination awareness campaigns and conducted roadshows and talks during the annual World Immunisation Week.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Information on NAIS is available on the Health Promotion Board's (HPB) HealthHub Portal.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: MOH is also planning a series of population-level vaccination awareness campaigns to increase the public's awareness on the importance of vaccination.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am very glad that the Ministry is doing all it can to encourage the take-up rate for vaccinations.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But may I know if the vaccination rates are lower, among our lower-income group?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Vaccination uptake is influenced by a number of factors.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: It includes awareness, importance of vaccinations, accessibility and affordability.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Hence, we hope to reduce the barriers for vaccinations and increase its uptake by extending subsidies for NAIS vaccinations.
